journeySteps.title: Register with us
journeySteps.copy: Call us or fill in the online form. Tell us whether you want to be seen on the NHS, privately, or a mix of both — most patients are.

journeySteps.title: Your first visit
journeySteps.copy: A full examination of your teeth and gums, plus a chat about your dental history and anything you are worried about. We take X-rays only if you need them.

journeySteps.title: Your written treatment plan
journeySteps.copy: Before any treatment starts, you get a written plan setting out what we recommend, what it costs, and what happens if you decide against any part of it.

whatToBring: Photo ID, such as a driving licence or passport
A list of any medicines you take, including ones you buy over the counter
Evidence of exemption from NHS charges, if this applies to you
Details of your previous dentist, if you have one, so we can request your records

newPatientOffer.title: New patient examination (private)
includes: An estimate for any further treatment

nervousPatients.intro: If you're nervous about the dentist, tell us — you won't be the only patient today who is. We would rather know than have you put off a visit.
accommodations: Book the first appointment slot of the day, before the waiting room fills up and before the day's schedule can overrun
Agree a stop signal with your dentist before we start, so you are always in control of when we pause
Ask for a walk-through of the surgery and instruments on a separate visit first, with nothing done that day
nervousPatients.sedationCopy: For some patients, sedation makes treatment more manageable. We can talk you through the options — from a mild relaxant tablet taken beforehand to intravenous sedation — and refer you to a specialist sedation service if your treatment needs it.
